# @verdent/auth-js

Verdent-managed Supabase Auth SDK and built-in browser UI.

The SDK owns the Google OAuth, email/password, sign-up OTP, and password-recovery
OTP flows. Pass an existing Supabase client; no authentication handlers are
required.

## Install

Configure the Verdent scope in your project's `.npmrc`:

```ini
@verdent:registry=https://npm.verdent.app
```

Then install the package normally:

```sh
npm install @supabase/supabase-js @verdent/auth-js
```

## Usage

```ts
import { createClient } from '@supabase/supabase-js'
import { createVerdentAuth } from '@verdent/auth-js'

const supabase = createClient(
  window.location.origin,
  'verdent-baas-key',
)

const auth = createVerdentAuth({ supabase })

auth.openSignInModal({
  redirectTo: window.location.origin,
  defaultEmail: '',
  theme: 'system',
  onSuccess(result) {
    console.log('Authenticated', result.action, result.user)
  },
})
```

`openSignInModal()` starts with Google and email entry. A valid email advances
to password login; sign-up and forgot-password views are managed internally.
Set `initialView` to `signUp` or `forgotPassword` to open another view first.
Successful login, sign-up, or password recovery closes the modal automatically.

## Localization

The built-in UI supports the same locales as the Verdent website:
`en`, `zh-CN`, `zh-Hant`, `ja`, `ko`, `es`, `pt`, `it`, `tr`, `de`, `fr`,
and `ar`.

English remains the default for backward compatibility. Pass a locale directly
or use `auto` to resolve `document.documentElement.lang` and browser preferences:

```ts
auth.openSignInModal({
  locale: 'auto',
  messages: {
    continueLabel: 'Custom continue label',
  },
})
```

Common variants such as `zh-TW`, `zh-HK`, `zh-Hans`, `pt-BR`, and `fr-CA` are
normalized to supported locales. Arabic automatically uses right-to-left
layout. Existing individual label options remain supported and take precedence
over `messages`.

Use `mountSignIn()` to render the same flow into an existing element:

```ts
const mounted = auth.mountSignIn('#auth-root', {
  initialView: 'signIn',
})

mounted.destroy()
```

## OAuth configuration

For Verdent-managed Supabase URLs, the SDK infers the project ref and trusted
OAuth broker. An explicit URL is only needed for a custom deployment:

```ts
const auth = createVerdentAuth({
  supabase,
  oauth: {
    authorizeUrl: 'https://custom-oauth.example.com/app/initiate',
    timeoutMs: 5 * 60 * 1000,
  },
})
```

Programmatic Google OAuth resolves only after the broker response is validated
and the returned session has been stored in the Supabase client:

```ts
const result = await auth.signInWithOAuth({
  provider: 'google',
  redirectTo: window.location.origin,
})
```

## Errors and lifecycle

Authentication errors are shown inline. Customize or observe them without
replacing the built-in authentication behavior:

```ts
auth.openSignInModal({
  formatErrorMessage(error) {
    return error instanceof Error ? error.message : 'Authentication failed.'
  },
  onError(error, context) {
    console.warn('Auth failure', context.action, error)
  },
  onClose(reason) {
    console.log(reason) // "success" or "dismissed"
  },
})
```

The password-recovery UI uses a recovery OTP. Configure the Verdent-managed
Supabase recovery email template to include the OTP token; recovery-link-only
templates are not supported by this release.

Branding is resolved from explicit options, then page metadata and favicon
links, then the Verdent fallback. `theme: 'system'` follows the browser color
scheme.

## Local demo

Set `VITE_SUPABASE_URL` and `VITE_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY`, then run:

```sh
pnpm install
pnpm dev
```

Append `?locale=zh-CN`, `?locale=zh-Hant`, `?locale=ar`, or `?locale=auto` to
the demo URL to preview localized UI.
